flashcards.q: What is test-time compute and why is it called a third scaling axis?
flashcards.a: Allocating more inference-time compute per query (long internal chains of thought, exploration, self-verification) to improve accuracy — a new axis beyond parameters+data (pretraining) and alignment (post-training). Accuracy climbs roughly logarithmically with thinking tokens; intelligence became a per-query dial.

flashcards.q: How do reasoning models differ from prompted chain-of-thought?
flashcards.a: Prompted CoT is a trick over a frozen policy: short chains, no training signal rewarding good reasoning. Reasoning models are trained via RL whose reward lands on final answers against verifiers, so the chain itself evolves — exploration, backtracking, and self-correction emerge because they correlate with correctness. The distinction is presence of a training loop, not formatting.

flashcards.q: Walk through what RL on chains of thought actually trains.
flashcards.a: Sample problems, generate full chains ending in answers, score final answers with verifiers (tests/exact-match/rubrics), update the policy toward chains that produced correct outcomes — R1 used GRPO (group-relative advantage ranking within sampled groups, no value network). Reward-on-outcomes-only lets chain structure evolve freely; backtracking emerges statistically, not by scripting.

flashcards.q: What did DeepSeek-R1-Zero demonstrate, and why did shipped R1 add SFT anyway?
flashcards.a: That strong reasoning chains can emerge from large-scale pure RL without supervised fine-tuning — falsifying assumptions that heavy SFT bootstrapping was required. But pure-RL training showed readability degradation and language mixing, so shipped R1 added a light cold-start SFT stage for readable, language-consistent traces.

flashcards.q: Quote the headline benchmark evidence for the reasoning-model jump.
flashcards.a: AIME 2024 math: GPT-4o-class ~13% vs o3-class ~96%, R1 at 79.8%. GPQA-Diamond: o3 87.7%, R1 71.5%. SWE-bench Verified: o3 ~71.7%, R1 49.2%. Codeforces: o3 ~2727, R1 2029. Plus o3's high-compute ARC-AGI runs on an anti-memorization benchmark (~tens of millions of tokens per problem).

flashcards.q: Why did DeepSeek-R1 matter beyond its scores?
flashcards.a: MIT-licensed open weights plus published recipe proved frontier-class reasoning was replicable outside frontier labs; R1-Zero showed pure RL sufficed; price reset to roughly 5% of o1's API; transparent <think> traces enabled inspection and distillation (small models trained on great traces beat bigger models without them); it turned reasoning access into a commoditization debate overnight. Note: replicable recipe ≠ cheap training.

flashcards.q: Explain the economics inversion in reasoning-model bills.
flashcards.a: Base-model bills are input-dominated (big context, short answer). Reasoner bills are output-dominated: e.g., ~500 input tokens vs ~5,000 output tokens where ~4,500 are hidden thinking you're billed for. Hard queries scale brutally: ~50,000 thinking tokens ≈ $0.40 at o3-class pricing; hardest-tier runs averaged ~57M tokens and ~14 min/question. Per-query cost becomes a distribution → budget tables and p95 alerting.

flashcards.q: Describe the test-time compute curve's shape and its practical corollaries.
flashcards.a: Approximately logarithmic: steep early gains, diminishing returns, plateau, sometimes degradation from overthinking loops. Corollaries: easy tasks saturate within hundreds of tokens while hard-solvable tasks have long tails; it composes with best-of-k/self-consistency sampling at multiplicative cost; log-shape makes budget-setting marginal-returns optimization — hence coarse effort tiers (minimal/low/medium/high) as the exposed interface.

flashcards.q: List where reasoning models LOSE to fast models, and why.
flashcards.a: Conversational chat (latency kills UX, no accuracy gain); content generation (style bottleneck, indistinguishable output at 10x cost); simple lookups (no benefit); orchestration-bound agent loops (wall-clock is tool calls/parsing); subjective/creative work; high-throughput latency-SLO pipelines. Plus overthinking: thousands of tokens where a fast model is correct in one pass, occasionally degrading instruction-following.

flashcards.q: Design hybrid routing for production — including failure handling.
flashcards.a: Classify queries (task class, complexity, fast-model confidence via logprobs/self-consistency); send ~90% to fast default; escalate on low confidence/hard classes/explicit demand; use reasoner-as-critic for drafts on critical paths; set per-task-class budgets from logged accuracy-vs-budget curves. Failure handling: token/time ceilings, loop detectors (repetition scores), fallback to fast model with honest uncertainty, p95 cost alerts.

flashcards.q: What is the chain-of-thought faithfulness problem?
flashcards.a: The visible chain isn't guaranteed to be the model's actual causal computation — RL shapes chains statistically toward rewarded outcomes, so traces may rationalize rather than explain. Chains are good telemetry, weak testimony: compliance/safety flows need outcome-level verification, not chain-inspection certificates. Visibility (R1's <think>) aids debugging/distillation but legibility ≠ faithfulness.

flashcards.q: Why don't reasoning models fix hallucination, and what does help?
flashcards.a: Hallucination is mostly a knowledge/retrieval problem; reasoning computes over available representations — a reasoner can build internally-consistent arguments from false premises. Helps: retrieval grounding, citation requirements, external outcome verification, calibrated abstention rewards, self-consistency checks. Reasoning DOES reduce manipulation-errors (multi-step arithmetic/logic). Know which error regime you're in before prescribing it.

flashcards.q: A team's agent calls a reasoner for every step, 30-60s per action. Restructure it.
flashcards.a: Separate thinking-bound from orchestration-bound steps: fast model executes routine steps; reserve the reasoner for initial planning on complex goals, verification/critic of consequential actions, and low-confidence recovery. Add streaming status UX, parallel independent tool calls, cached context, per-step-type budget caps. Expect the reasoner touching ~10-20% of steps at equal task success.

flashcards.q: Where does test-time scaling head next, and what would falsify the paradigm?
flashcards.a: Directions: efficiency compression ($1M-class capability at $-class cost via trace compression/distills), adaptive stopping (learning when to stop), hybrid fast/deep toggling, agentic reasoning across hours of tool use. Open: how far curves extend (30h of thinking unmapped), generalization past verifiable domains, monitorability. Falsification: universal early flattening or discovery that gains were benchmark-specific search rather than transferable deliberation.

flashcards.q: Why evaluate reasoning models on private held-out sets rather than public benchmarks?
flashcards.a: Public benchmarks saturate quickly and leak into training data (contamination), and vendor-reported scores vary with undisclosed compute configurations. Private held-out task suites measure the completion behavior you actually ship; leaderboard rank predicts your task performance poorly. Also cite benchmark numbers with source-and-date plus configuration tier when quoting them at all.
